name: TAPNext
plain: TAPNext (Google DeepMind, 2025): tracks any point through a video, online one frame at a time, as next-token prediction with a ViT + linear-recurrence (RG-LRU) backbone; BootsTAPNext-B and the long-video TAPNext++. Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: TAPNext (Zholus, Doersch, Yang, Koppula et al., Google DeepMind 2025): tracking any point as next-token prediction. A TRecViT-B (12 blocks, each a gated linear recurrence over time per token and a ViT layer over the tokens of a frame) reads 8 x 8 patches of 256 x 256 frames plus one token per query point and predicts, frame by frame, the point's position (512-bin classification, windowed soft-argmax) and whether it is visible. Online: each frame only sees the past.

papers.title: TAPNext: Tracking Any Point (TAP) as Next Token Prediction
TAPNext++: What's Next for Tracking Any Point (TAP)?

limitations: Online, causal: a point is tracked from its query frame on; in frames before it the model has no information (the tracks there are its guess, with a low visibility). Query on the first frame, or run the reversed video for the backward part.
Frames are resized to 256 x 256 (the training size), whatever their size and aspect ratio.
One video per call; all queries of a call share the video.
task_io: Input: a video (its frames in order) and query points `(t, x, y)`. Output: the position of every query in every frame and the probability that it is visible there.

variants.name: tapnext

licence.training_note: Upstream: TAPNext is trained on synthetic Kubric MOVi-F sequences and fine-tuned with BootsTAP self-training on unlabelled real videos (not released); TAPNext++ is further fine-tuned on PointOdyssey and Kubric-1024 (1024-frame synthetic sequences). variants.input_size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

kernels.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

original16.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls
original16.note: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); upstream TAPNext, online one frame per call; frames resized to 256 x 256 (antialiased bilinear)
